A.explanation: This inverts stress and strain and mishandles the $10^8$ and $10^{-3}$ multipliers, giving $1/E$ with wrong powers of ten.

B.explanation: This is approximately strain divided by stress, $1.4 \times 10^{-3} / 2.1 \times 10^8$, which is the reciprocal of the Young modulus.

C.explanation: This divides $2.1$ by $1.4$ but ignores the $10^8$ on stress and $10^{-3}$ on strain, so it is too small by a factor of $10^3$.

D.explanation: Dividing the limit-of-proportionality stress $2.1 \times 10^8 \text{ Pa}$ by the strain $1.4 \times 10^{-3}$ gives $1.5 \times 10^{11} \text{ Pa}$.

hints: Notice the graph is straight only up to stress $2.1$ on the $10^8 \text{ Pa}$ scale and strain $1.4$ on the $10^{-3}$ scale, so use that end point for the gradient.
Recall Young modulus is the gradient of the initial straight line: $E = \text{stress} / \text{strain}$ while Hooke's law holds.
Convert the axis readings first to $2.1 \times 10^8 \text{ Pa}$ and $1.4 \times 10^{-3}$, then divide and check the power of ten is near $10^{11} \text{ Pa}$ for a metal wire.
walkthrough: Identify the linear region on the stress-strain graph. It runs from the origin to stress $= 2.1 \times 10^8 \text{ Pa}$ at strain $= 1.4 \times 10^{-3}$.
State the rule: Young modulus $E = \text{stress} / \text{strain}$ from the gradient of the straight-line part only, not the later curved part.
Substitute the values with units: $E = (2.1 \times 10^8 \text{ Pa}) / (1.4 \times 10^{-3})$.
Calculate: $2.1/1.4 = 1.5$ and $10^8/10^{-3} = 10^{11}$, so $E = 1.5 \times 10^{11} \text{ Pa}$, which has the correct unit of pressure.
